To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the membrane fatty acid compositions of zoo giraffes and their wild counterparts differ significantly in the levels of polyunsaturated fatty acids; and (b) the fatty acid composition of brain membranes of the zoo animals is significantly different from that in the wild animals, and the changes in fatty acid composition in brain membranes are similar to those that have been used experimentally to render animals susceptible to BSE.
the membrane composition of zoo giraffe is different to that of wild animals.

the membrane fatty acid compositions in giraffes from their natural habitat and in zoo giraffes were different and that this difference is similar to changes seen experimentally to make rats susceptible to encephalomyeilitis and cattle susceptible to encephalomelacia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of nutrition in the aetiology of bovine spongiform encephalopathy.
the effect of changes in diet on the membrane composition of the brain.
the possibility that changes in the fatty acid content of ruminant tissues may have been responsible for the appearance of BSE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence is not sufficient to prove a causal relationship between bovine spongiform encephalopathy and bovine spongigorm encephalopathy.
there is no direct evidence that nutritional changes have contributed to BSE.
the evidence is consistent with a nutritional hypothesis for bovine spongiform encephalopathy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a change in the feeding style of cattle from a natural grass diet to a diet of grain, animal proteins, and other nitrogenous supplements has altered the fatty acid composition of cell membranes.

the changes in animal feeding style that were made during the last century to improve the growth and productivity of farm livestock have had an adverse effect on their health and welfare, and that these changes are likely to be the underlying cause of BSE and the new variant of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease in humans.
the nutritional contribution to bovine spongiform encephalopathy may be due to the effect of animal protein and nitrogen supplements on the membrane fatty acid content of ruminant tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the membrane changes seen in cattle and other animals fed animal protein are similar to those seen in animals made susceptible to encephalomalacias and encephalopathies.
the membrane composition of ruminants is highly sensitive to changes in the feeding style.
it is possible to alter the membrane composition and hence the membrane stability of ruminant animals by altering the feed.
